MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Sex: Male
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Infertility evaluation for oligospermia
Clinical History: Patient presents with oligospermia identified on semen analysis

TEST PERFORMED
Y Chromosome Microdeletion Analysis by Multiplex PCR

METHODOLOGY
Multiplex PCR amplification was performed to detect Y chromosome microdeletions associated with male infertility. The following sequence-tagged sites (STS) markers were analyzed:
- AZFa region: sY84, sY86
- AZFb region: sY127, sY134
- AZFc region: sY254, sY255
- Yp11.31: SRY (sex-determining region Y)
- Xp22.2: Amelogenin X
- Yp11.2: Amelogenin Y

DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis. Internal controls were included to verify DNA quality and PCR efficiency.

RESULTS

Y Chromosome Microdeletion Panel:

AZFa region:
- sY84: PRESENT
- sY86: PRESENT

AZFb region:
- sY127: PRESENT
- sY134: PRESENT

AZFc region:
- sY254: PRESENT
- sY255: PRESENT

Control Markers:
- SRY: PRESENT
- Amelogenin X: PRESENT
- Amelogenin Y: PRESENT

RESULT: NO DELETIONS DETECTED

INTERPRETATION
No complete AZFa, AZFb or AZFc deletions were detected. All tested markers are present. This result excludes complete deletion of the AZFa, AZFb or AZFc regions as a cause of the patient's oligospermia.

TEST LIMITATIONS
This assay detects complete deletions of AZF regions based on the absence of specific STS markers. Small microdeletions within AZF regions flanking the marker sequences or deletions outside the AZF regions would not be detected by this assay. Partial AZF deletions involving sequences between tested markers may also be missed. This test does not detect point mutations or other sequence variants.

BACKGROUND
Y chromosome microdeletions are found in approximately 10-15% of men with severe oligospermia or azoospermia. The AZF (Azoospermia Factor) regions contain genes critical for spermatogenesis. Complete deletions of AZFa or AZFb typically result in azoospermia with spermatogenic arrest, while AZFc deletions may present with variable phenotypes ranging from oligospermia to azoospermia. Men with AZFc deletions may still achieve biological paternity through assisted reproductive techniques, though male offspring will inherit the deletion.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. G-banded chromosome analysis and cystic fibrosis gene mutation testing results are pending and will be reported separately
2. Consider additional genetic evaluation if karyotype and CFTR testing are negative
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and reproductive options

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
